translation:
(Shi Ruo says: The medicine is not used after the nosebleed; rather, when one should sweat, using it then one does not have the nosebleed. It is only because one did not sweat first that one has the nosebleed.)

The Guizhi Tang formula: Guizhi (cinnamon twig), Shaoyao (peony, each 3 liang), Gancao (licorice, roasted, 2 liang), Shengjiang (fresh ginger, 3 liang), Dazao (jujube, 12 pieces, broken).

The above five ingredients, cut. With 7 sheng of water, boil and take 3 sheng, remove the dregs, take 1 sheng warm, and after a moment eat 1 sheng of thin gruel to assist the medicinal strength, and cover to obtain slight sweat. Avoid raw scallion, seaweed, and cabbage. (Same as Jiyan, Beiji, Wenzhong, and Fan Wang. In Zhongjing's Shanghan Lun, this formula can be taken by those whose disease is on the exterior on the sixth or seventh day.)

Again, in cold damage of five or six days, those who vomit and have fever have the Chaihu Tang signs complete; but if one purges with other medicines and the Chaihu signs are still present, one can give the Chaihu Tang. Although this has already been purged, it is not a counterflow; one will certainly steam and tremble and retreat, then sweat and resolve.
